report.summary: Chunk 3 of 3 of daedalus/council/bus.py: public append APIs (append_round, append_turn, append_roster) and reading/verification functions (load_transcript, transcript_head, read_anchor, verify_chain).

handoff.purpose: Implement public append, read, and verify chain APIs for council transcript.

symbols.name: append_round
symbols.note: Chains a whole round of turns, normalizing and sorting them.

symbols.name: append_turn
symbols.note: Convenience wrapper for appending a single turn.

symbols.name: append_roster
symbols.note: Chains roster accounting with derived counts.

symbols.name: load_transcript
symbols.note: Reads all records from a store file, skipping torn lines.

symbols.name: transcript_head
symbols.note: Returns record count and head entry SHA from the file.

symbols.name: read_anchor
symbols.note: Reads the anchor file, returns None if missing or corrupt.

symbols.name: verify_chain
symbols.note: Walks the chain and returns (ok, failures) with detailed checks.

claims.text: Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with ``seq`` assigned here -- so reversed completion order yields a byte-identical chain head.
claims.why: The sorting key in the code sorts by actor, role, status, and canonical_body_json, not just actor id. Also 'secret-floored' and 'seq assigned here' are not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug that would double a voice, and a missing participant must be recorded as an ``unavailable`` turn rather than skipped.
claims.why: Code checks for duplicates after normalizing and raises ValueError if any actor appears more than once (excluding 'council.redacted.redacted').

claims.text: Canonical body is the final tiebreak so the order is TOTAL even when two anonymised refusal receipts collapse to the same actor: chaining must not inherit wall-clock completion order from anywhere.
claims.why: The sort key includes canonical_body_json as the last element, ensuring total order.

claims.text: Chain a single turn (a one-participant round). Convenience over :func:`append_round`; prefer the round form so ordering stays deterministic.
claims.why: append_turn calls append_round with a single-turn list, as described.

claims.text: Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller: '3 of 4' and '2 of 2' must not be able to render as the same string, and a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council.
claims.why: The code computes requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, duplicate_classes, degraded from the normalized participants, not from caller input.

claims.text: Duplicate weights are detected over everyone SEATED (that is when the clone was let in); the distinct-class count is over those who actually RESPONDED, because an unavailable participant contributes no voice and a class count that includes it overstates the independence on the record.
claims.why: seated_classes includes outcomes 'seated', 'responded', 'refused'; heard_classes only includes 'responded'. duplicate_classes is computed from seated_classes; distinct_classes from heard_classes.

claims.text: Read all records, skipping a torn tail line (never fatal). Missing is [].
claims.why: Code returns [] if file does not exist; loops over lines, skipping empty and JSONDecodeError lines (torn/corrupt).

claims.text: ``(record_count, head_entry_sha)`` -- the tail anchor, recomputed from the file. Compare against :func:`read_anchor` to catch a truncation.
claims.why: Returns (len(records), records[-1].get('entry_sha') if records else None).

claims.text: Three independent checks per line: * ``body_sha`` recomputed over the canonical body -- catches a content edit; * ``entry_sha`` recomputed over ``(prev, stored body_sha, ts)`` -- catches a back-dated ts or a rewritten link where body_sha WAS updated; * ``prev`` equals the previous line's ``entry_sha`` -- catches a deleted or reordered line (the survivor points at a vanished predecessor).
claims.why: The code calls _body_sha(rec) and _entry_sha(prev, stored_body, ts), but these functions are not defined in this chunk, so we cannot verify they recompute as described.

claims.text: TAIL truncation is the one deletion a per-line walk cannot catch (a valid chain's prefix is a valid chain), so the persisted anchor is consulted by default and a shortfall in count or head is NAMED.
claims.why: Code reads anchor if use_anchor is True and no explicit expected_count/head; then compares n_records and prev_entry_sha to expected values.

claims.text: Explicit ``expected_count`` / ``expected_head`` override it; ``use_anchor=False`` verifies linkage only.
claims.why: If use_anchor is True and expected_count/head are None, anchor is used. Otherwise, provided values are used. use_anchor=False skips anchor reading.

observations.what: append_round sorts by (actor, role, status, canonical_body_json), not just actor id as implied in docstring.
append_roster uses 'refused' outcome in seated_classes but not in heard_classes; docstring says duplicate weights detected over everyone SEATED.
verify_chain's checks rely on external functions _body_sha and _entry_sha not defined in this chunk.
